glosses: het iemand iets mededelen

examples.text: Raphael Mutiku, die na de aardbeving voor Oxfam instond voor de installatie van watervoorziening in Haïti, kreeg in juni 2010 een laatste geschreven verwittiging wegens grensoverschrijdend seksueel gedrag. Zes maanden later vernam de ngo dat de veertiger jonge vrouwen zou betalen voor seks in zijn woning.

Minister Schippers (Zorg, VVD) heeft op de valreep het debat over winstuitkeringen in de ziekenhuiszorg, dat vandaag zou worden gehouden, uitgesteld. De minister bood de Tweede Kamer haar excuses aan voor de „late verwittiging”. Schippers schrijft dat ze tot de conclusie gekomen is „dat onderdelen van het wetsvoorstel nog nader moeten worden onderzocht”.

glosses: The act of observing; perception.

examples.text: He took no notice of the changes, and went on as though nothing had happened.

Athelstan Arundel walked home[…], foaming and raging. […] He walked the whole way, walking through crowds, and under the noses of dray-horses, carriage-horses, and cart-horses, without taking the least notice of them.
How ready is envy to mingle with the notices which we take of other persons?

glosses: A written or printed announcement.

examples.text: Shall we post a notice about the new policy?
A notice was attached to the building reminding the residents about the five hour water shortage that was happening today.
I always read the death notices in the paper.

glosses: A formal notification or warning.

examples.text: The sidewalk adjacent to the damaged bridge stonework shall be closed until further notice.

glosses: Advance notification of termination of employment, given by an employer to an employee or vice versa.

examples.text: I gave her her mandatory two weeks' notice and sacked her.
I can't work here any longer. I'm giving notice.

glosses: A published critical review of a play or the like.

examples.text: The first-night audience, yes. The first-night reviewers, not exactly. The notices have so far been mixed, only The Financial Times having delivered itself of an unequivocal rave.

glosses: Prior notification.

examples.text: I don't mind if you want to change the venue; just give me some notice first, OK?
I have been with your father and given him notice that the Duke of Cornwall and Regan his duchess will be here with him this night.

glosses: Attention; respectful treatment; civility.
To remark upon; to mention.

examples.text: Numberless are the arguments […] that men have used morally and physically, to degrade the sex. I must notice a few.

glosses: To become aware of; to observe.

examples.text: Did you notice the flowers in her yard?
So you punched out a window for ventilation. Was that before or after you noticed you were standing in a lake of gasoline?

[The researchers] noticed many of their pieces of [plastic marine] debris sported surface pits around two microns across. Such pits are about the size of a bacterial cell. Closer examination showed that some of these pits did, indeed, contain bacteria, […].

glosses: To lavish attention upon; to treat (someone) favourably.

examples.text: She would notice her; she would improve her; she would detach her from her bad acquaintance, and introduce her into good society; she would form her opinions and her manners.

glosses: To be noticeable; to show.

examples.text: The blackness didn't notice so much when she was born; but it's unmistakeable now.

glosses: A communication, or what is communicated; any concept or information conveyed.

examples.text: We've just received an urgent message from the President.
He received a message telling him to update his laptop.
I have a message from God unto thee.

No matter how early I came down, I would find him on the veranda, smoking cigarettes, or otherwise his man would be there with a message to say that his master would shortly join me if I would kindly wait.

glosses: An underlying theme or conclusion to be drawn from something.

examples.text: The main message of the novel is that time heals all wounds.

Even without hovering drones, a lurking assassin, a thumping score and a denouement, the real-life story of Edward Snowden, a rogue spy on the run, could be straight out of the cinema. But, as with Hollywood, the subplots and exotic locations may distract from the real message: America’s discomfort and its foes’ glee.

glosses: An errand.

examples.text: I had been on a message for my father, and was walking home along the road, when I saw a tall, fine lassie coming over the bogland on the right hand side of the road.

glosses: See messages (“groceries, shopping”).
To send a message to; to transmit a message to, e.g. as text via a cell phone.

examples.text: Just message me for directions.
I messaged her about the concert.

glosses: To send (something) as a message; usually refers to electronic messaging.

examples.text: She messaged me the information yesterday.
Please message the final report by fax.

glosses: To send a message or messages; to be capable of sending messages.

examples.text: We've implemented a new messaging service.
The runaway computer program was messaging non-stop.

glosses: To bear as a message.
present participle of warn

examples.text: Although the Celebrity was almost impervious to sarcasm, he was now beginning to exhibit visible signs of uneasiness,[…]. It was with a palpable relief that he heard the first warning notes of the figure.

glosses: The action of the verb warn; an instance of warning someone.

examples.text: “[…] Churchill, my dear fellow, we have such greedy sharks, and wolves in lamb's clothing. Oh, dear, there's so much to tell you, so many warnings to give you, but all that must be postponed for the moment.”
Without much warning, a deep voice addressed the crowd, calling for a reverent silence as the Texans who died at the Alamo battle were named.

glosses: Something spoken or written that is intended to warn.

examples.text: The boss gave him a warning that he would be fired if he did not desist from his behaviour.

Risk is everywhere. From tabloid headlines insisting that coffee causes cancer (yesterday, of course, it cured it) to stern government warnings about alcohol and driving, the world is teeming with goblins.

glosses: Used to warn of danger in signs and notices.
A declaration or remark.

examples.text: make a statement
publish a statement
utter a statement

glosses: A presentation of opinion or position.
A document that summarizes financial activity.

examples.text: a bank statement

glosses: An instruction in a computer program, especially one that returns no value, as opposed to a function call.

examples.text: In this section we will examine BASIC's primary statement for repeating a string of statements under program control: the FOR statement. Another statement, the NEXT statement, is always used with a FOR statement.
However, it is the responsibility of the programmer to ensure that the control ultimately reaches the last statement of the range.

glosses: Decisive.

examples.text: Gabriel Martinelli scored a dramatic late winner as Arsenal earned a statement victory over defending Premier League champions Manchester City at Emirates Stadium.

glosses: To provide an official document of a proposition, especially in the UK, a Statement of Special Educational Needs.
Information.
Avertissement.
